cases.detail: Verilator executes always @* at time zero with declaration-initialized inputs for both retained and completely assigned outputs, changing q before a sensitivity event. IEEE 1800-2023 6.8 initializes static declarations before initial/always processes start, and 9.2.2.2.2 requires always @* to wait for a sensitivity change. Icarus passes the unchanged shared assertions; the adapter-free sources reproduce the Verilator failures.

cases.detail: Verilator executes the self-reading always_comb latch more than once after seed/en change: the shared case expects q=1 and observes q=3. An adapter-free reproduction expects q=1 and observes q=2 in Verilator, while Icarus observes q=1 and passes unchanged-input and overwritten-read sensitivity checks. IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1 excludes the written q expression from implicit sensitivity; its own write must not retrigger this process. Celox and Icarus pass the original shared assertions.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 reports DIDNOTCONVERGE in the settle region for these self-reading @* / always_latch processes, before the timed pulse assertions. The unchanged adapter-free sources also fail to settle, while Icarus 13.0 completes both. IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.3 applies the always_comb written-expression sensitivity exclusion (9.2.2.2.1) to always_latch; an @* procedure waits at its event control and does not wait on its own blocking body writes (9.2.2.1, 9.4.2.2). A self-write must not produce an endless activation loop. This exclusion concerns the observed nonconvergence, not arbitrary ordering between independent active-region processes.

cases.detail: Verilator wakes always_comb/always_latch when globals read only inside called task bodies change, failing the assertion that both outputs remain zero without an argument change. IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1 adds task arguments but excludes task contents from implicit sensitivity; 9.2.2.3 applies the same rules to always_latch. Icarus passes both the unchanged-global-sensitivity assertion and the later argument-change assertion in the exact adapter-free shared source.
